newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols steady, await jobs data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols steady, await jobs data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. T-bond options were little changed, showing little reaction to the second leg of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony, dealers said.

Although the underlying bond market bounced from early lows and clawed back into positive territory as the testimony began, volatilities were underpinned by caution ahead of Friday's February employment report, they said.
Greenspan's remarks before a House banking subcommittee was unchanged from what was delivered last last week to the Senate Banking Committee in the first leg of the testimony.

A brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) said volatilities were holding steady probably because most traders believed the mild bond rally was a technical bounce and not a wholehearted effort to rise higher.
"There was some good selling in the morning," he said of the bond market. "So maybe people are piggy-banking some of those stuff. The market has been weak for the last few sessions, too."
Implied volatilities for April and June T-bond futures options were virtually unchanged from Tuesday at around 10.2 9.9 percent respectively.
Option traffic in the CBOT pit was moderate, with a lot of medium-sized spreads and combos going through, traders said.

There was some big put buying in the morning, reflecting growing concerns of an imminent credit tightening. A big investment bank was said to have bought 5,000 contracts of April 106-108 put spreads and then another 2,500 of June 106-108 put spread.

The shorter end of the yield curve also saw volatilities steady to firmer in nervous trading as a further flattening of the curve was seen inevitable whether or not Fed hikes rates soon, traders said.

"Everyone is expecting something on the floor," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME). "Even though the net change in prices was very small, it was still very loud on the floor."
Implied volatilities for CME June and September Eurodollar futures options stood little changed at around 10.5 and 13.9 percent respectively.
Traders expected the Eurodollar market to continue trading narrowly on Thursday, not reacting too much on the weekly jobless claims and January factory orders data.
"I don't think people are going to jump up and down on that," he added. "Clearly, people are positioning themselves for Friday's numbers."
